mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds rate above 5.25% in the month preceding the forecast period is associated with a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return due to tightened financial conditions.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.25% in the month prior
regime_hint: tightening cycle after a period of easing
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero when FEDFUNDS > 5.25%, p > 0.05 (t-test).

mechanism_narrative: Rising unemployment claims (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in consumer pay growth (HOUST) predict negative 60-day S&P 500 forward returns as labor market weakness dampens corporate optimism.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases while HOUST decreases in the same month
failure_condition: Rank IC > 0.05 over 60-day horizon when PAYEMS up and HOUST down, or 60-day returns are positive despite the signal.

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly decline in industrial production (INDPRO) exceeding 2% suggests weakening demand, leading to positive 20-day S&P 500 forward returns as market anticipates a rebound.
failure_condition: INDPRO does not decline by >2% over the next 6 months, or 20-day returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained acceleration in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) above 3% for two consecutive months predicts negative 5-day S&P 500 forward returns as investors anticipate rate hikes that suppress equity valuations.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL increases at a rate >3% month-over-month for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not negative when CPIAUCSL accelerates >3% MoM, or inflation decelerates within 2 months.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate falls below 4% (UNRATE) while FEDFUNDS remains below 4%, a 20-day positive S&P 500 forward return is expected as policy becomes more accommodative.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4% and FEDFUNDS < 4% in the same month
regime_hint: labor market tightening coupled with low policy rates
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not significantly positive when both conditions hold (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in monthly pay growth (PAYEMS) above 300,000 suggests wage inflation, which is associated with negative 60-day S&P 500 forward returns as investors anticipate higher labor costs and slower growth.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS crosses above 300,000 in the month
failure_condition: 60-day returns are not negative when PAYEMS > 300,000 (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in manufacturing activity (RSAFS) below 400 billion for three consecutive months predicts a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as market anticipates a supply-side recovery.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not positive when RSAFS remains below 400B for >3 months (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During a regime of persistent monetary easing (FEDFUNDS < 4%), a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return is expected when the 12-month change in consumer prices (CPIAUCSL) is negative, indicating deflationary pressure.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 4% and CPIAUCSL monthly change < 0 over the past 12 months
failure_condition: 60-day returns are not positive when both triggers are met (p > 0.05).
